title: We are your community paper
author: Unknown
thematic_categories: Press & Media Criticism, Audience & Public Engagement, Journalism Theory & Practice
summary: Editorial about the role of community newspapers in local civic life. The piece references a speech by NYU professor Jay Rosen about the relationship between newspapers and communities, arguing that newspapers create connections between people who share common concerns and that the domain of the newspaper is public life.
excerpt: Once again, let's cite Professor Rosen. 'The more people feel they have in common, the greater the newspaper's power to communicate... News matters to people who share common understandings, common spaces and common concerns — public concerns. The domain of the newspaper is — and always will be — public life.'
pull_quote: The domain of the newspaper is — and always will be — public life.
tags: newspaper clipping, community journalism, public life, newspapers, 1990s
copyright: © The Cashmere Valley Record. Available via newspapers.com.
notes: Source PDF: The_Cashmere_Valley_Record_1990_10_24_2.pdf. Page 2. Editorial extensively quotes Jay Rosen's speech about community newspapers and public life. An early example of Rosen's influence on community journalism thinking.

title: Neil Postman, 72; Author warned of technology threats
author: Elaine Woo
thematic_categories: Journalism Education, Press & Media Criticism, Technology & Digital Media
key_concepts: Media criticism, Technology and society, NYU, Media ecology
summary: Full obituary for Neil Postman, the NYU professor and media critic who warned about technology's effects on education and culture. Postman was Jay Rosen's doctoral advisor and shaped his intellectual formation. The article details Postman's career at NYU where he taught for 44 years, his influential books, and his founding of NYU's media ecology program. It also mentions a quote from Postman noting that he was 'a New York University professor' connected to media education and criticism.
excerpt: Neil Postman, a gadfly educator and social critic whose writings about the pernicious effects of technology in American society were a constant source of angst... according to a spokesman for New York University, where Mr. Postman taught for 44 years... He began teaching at NYU in 1959 and in 1971 founded its media ecology program to study how modes of communication affect human perception and interaction.
pull_quote: 'What is the problem to which this is the solution?' he asked of the bewildered and sometimes cowed consumers forced to contend with changes.

notes: Source PDF: The_Los_Angeles_Times_2003_10_12_Page_166.pdf. Page 166 (B14). Original Los Angeles Times obituary for Neil Postman, Jay Rosen's doctoral advisor at NYU.
